text:
Anya Patel: Quick design check — I pushed a compact-range mock for the latency panel (figma: https://figma.com/file/abc123). Idea: collapse the timepicker into a single line with an optional expanded drawer, and add a "quick compare" pill to toggle p50/p95 side-by-side. Thoughts?

Mike Chen: Love the space savings. main worry: discoverability. if it’s collapsed by default, people might not realize the compare exists. can we surface it with a tiny badge? :thinking_face:

Jo Rivera: badge + a subtle pulse the first time users land on the dashboard could work. also suggest a keyboard hotkey (T) to expand the drawer. saves clicks for power users.

Olivia Gomez: accessibility note — heatmap colors need to be colorblind-safe. recommend using a diverging palette with a mono pattern fallback. also add numeric values in the tooltip so screenreader users can get p95 counts.

Kevin B: from infra side — sampling defaults are going to be important. if default sampling is too aggressive the p95 will be biased. can we show sample size + estimated CI inline? e.g. "Shown samples: 1,240 (±6% at 95% CI)" so folks know how stable the metric is.

design-bot: preview deployed to staging -> https://staging.redwood.design/latency/compact-range (expires in 48h) :rocket:

Anya Patel: nice — copying proposed microcopy for the sampling control:
```
Label: Shown samples
Helper: Controls the percentage of traces visualized. Lower samples = faster rendering, smaller statistical confidence.
Default: 5% (auto-adapt to traffic)
```
Also thinking of a small info icon that opens a 1-line explainer with a link to docs.

Mike Chen: can we tweak the label to "Displayed samples"? feels a bit clearer to non-stat folks. otherwise +1.

Jo Rivera: minor layout nits — when quick-compare is on, stack the p50 and p95 cards with a thin divider instead of different backgrounds. keeps visual weight equal. Also add aria-labels to the toggle:
```
aria-label="Toggle quick compare: show p50 and p95 side-by-side"
```

Olivia Gomez: focus states look faint on the mock — need 3:1 contrast min for the focus ring against background per our a11y baseline. also ensure the time scrubber has keyboard scrubbing (arrow keys step by 1s/1min depending on zoom).

Kevin B: cost indicator idea — show a tiny token-cost estimate next to the sampling slider (e.g. "est. cost: $0.02/min"). infra can provide a fast approximation via the metrics service. would help product teams make tradeoffs quickly.

Anya Patel: love the cost + CI suggestions. next steps: Mike — finalize microcopy (assign to you), Jo — add keyboard shortcut affordance + aria strings, Olivia — heatmap palette + focus states, Kevin — sample size + cost API hook. I’ll update the figma and push a second preview. please react with :+1: when you’re cool with this plan.

Mike Chen: +1
Jo Rivera: +1
Olivia Gomez: +1
Kevin B: +1

Anya Patel: leaving one more thought — for mobile, collapse should auto-expand when tapping the latency card for low-friction discoverability. we can test in the next usability pass.

Jo Rivera: noted — will include mobile behavior in the handoff doc.

Kevin B: quick question: do we want the default quick-compare off for new workspaces? avoids surprise costs.

Anya Patel: yes — default off, with an onboarding nudge showing benefits and cost/CI implications. thanks everyone — will update the figma and post the new preview link here.
